messages:
Maya Chen: Heads up — we're seeing GPU provisioning delays in eu-west regions. root cause looks like NVMe health checkpoint jitter on ephemeral nodes, causing attach/format to timeout and k8s to hold pods in Pending.
Ollie Park: any errors in the node logs?
Maya Chen: yes, attaching snippets below. pattern: repeated checkpoint flush stalls ~200-500ms then backoff, IO queue saturates, systemd-udev churn.
Maya Chen: ```
[kernel] nvme0: checkpoint: flush took 430ms, qdepth 128
[systemd] dev-sda: re-evaluating, format timed out
[containerd] attach failed: device busy
```
Ryan Patel: ugh. are these older drives or recent firmware?
Maya Chen: mix — a handful of hosts on the older batch (s/n prefix G4X) show worse numbers, but some newer ones spike during our nightly scrub windows. scrub overlap looks correlated.
Ollie Park: scrub window? we run aggressive scrub on 03:00-04:30 UTC in eu-west1. that's when provision requests spike for scheduled batch jobs.
Maya Chen: exact. hypothesis: scrub + continuous batching during morning ramp -> transient iops burst -> nvme checkpoint jitter -> attach timeouts -> provisioning queue backs up -> autoscaler keeps spinning new pods -> capacity hit.
SRE Pager: incident created: INC-2026-0221. pinging storage team. escalation to oncall infra.
Ryan Patel: short-term mitigation: can we shift scrub to lower-iops slice or add randomized jitter across AZs? also reduce per-node scrub concurrency.
Ollie Park: agree. I'll open a change to: 1) reduce scrub concurrency from 8->2, 2) randomize start +/- 15m per host, 3) throttle scrub IO to 40% of baseline. rolling start in 10m.
Maya Chen: also recommend a canary to drain one host type (older firmware) and repro provisioning under load, to see if firmware swap fixes.
Ryan Patel: cost note — if we add capacity while this persists we'll pay extra reserved-hours. prefer to throttle scrubs first.
Maya Chen: temporary policy update: for eu-west regions we will: pause full-window scrubs for 4 hours, apply throttling patch, and re-evaluate nightly. If repro confirms firmware regression we'll schedule batch firmware push next maintenance window.
infra-bot: change request created: CHG-8472 by Ollie Park — scrub concurrency reduction. status: scheduled (in 10 minutes).
Ollie Park: rolling the change now. monitoring dashboards: nvme latency, attach latency, and pending pod count. will update in thread.
Maya Chen: thanks. if we see sustained attach failures after throttle, we'll start draining affected hosts and replace with new pool.
SRE Pager: update: engineers paged. will follow up with postmortem if incident escalates. :mag:
